status.label: Shell-history integration boundary
status.detail: Run passes the initial command as a shell startup argument; terminal interactive history is a separate store.

next_action.label: Explain history ownership
next_action.reason: Distinguish an enhancement to interactive shell history from PowerToys Run's own query history.

judgment.rationale: The report asks for a command passed during process startup to become an interactive shell history entry. Current Shell plugin startup arguments explain the behavior; the cited bot matches concern Run's own history, which is different. A cross-shell history integration needs an explicit enhancement contract, not a demonstrated regression fix.
evidence: The report names 0.81.1, PowerShell 7.4.3 and Windows Terminal 1.20.11381.0 and describes Up-arrow history after Shell-plugin launch.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Microsoft.Plugin.Shell/Main.cs: PrepareProcessStartInfo uses cmd /k or PowerShell -NoExit -C, including inside wt.exe.
The Shell plugin also maintains its own _settings.Count history, separate from the launched shell's interactive input.
Inspected #21991 and #33403: they concern PowerToys query/history collection, not terminal-session Up-arrow history.
judgment.recommended_action: Explain the separate history stores and let maintainers decide whether shell-specific interactive-history integration should be an enhancement.

fix_assessment.rationale: No history regression or broken existing shell-history integration is demonstrated: the launcher passes startup arguments, not interactive keystrokes. Adding entries safely across CMD, PowerShell and PSReadLine would require a new explicit behavior/privacy contract.

issue_context.summary: Commands launched through Run's Shell plugin execute, but the user cannot recall the initial command with the new shell session's Up-arrow history.
known_information: The desired history belongs to the launched shell session/tab, not Run's search history.
The report supplies versions and short reproduction steps.
The only comment is an automated similarity list.
The live issue remains open, labeled Issue-Bug and unassigned.
inferences: The startup-argument versus interactive-input distinction accounts for the symptom without implying that execution failed.
A shell-specific history integration could be useful, but its desired persistence and privacy semantics need a maintainer decision.
issue_context.analysis: Do not mark the bot's history matches as duplicate fixes or conflate query storage with PSReadLine/CMD interactive history. A maintainer-facing scope explanation is sufficient for this lightweight pass.
initial_investigation: Read the full report and sole comment.
Verified current upstream Shell.Main.PrepareProcessStartInfo builds /k and -NoExit -C startup commands and keeps a separate Run-side history.
Read #21991 and #33403 to establish why those matches do not resolve this issue; the inspected timeline contains no concrete fix.

comment.body: Thanks for the clear Up-arrow reproduction and shell/Terminal versions. Run currently sends the initial command as a shell startup argument (for example cmd /k or PowerShell -NoExit -C), rather than entering it at an interactive prompt. The new shell owns its interactive history, separately from Run's own command/query history. Consequently the bot-linked Run-history issues do not cover this request. Supporting recall of startup commands would need an explicit shell-specific integration, including which history store is updated and whether commands persist. Maintainers can consider that as an enhancement; the report does not establish a regression in an existing interactive-history feature.
